title: Ferris wheel heights
concept: sin 30° = 1/2 and sin 60° is about 0.87, not 1: height above the axle divided by spoke length, measured on a turning Ferris wheel.
kept: Ferris wheel showing how high you are as it turns
Sine as opposite over hypotenuse (height over spoke)
Fair / sunset look: dusk sky bands, sun, dark ground
The friend's likely mistake (sin 60 = 1) is the wrong-guess option '20 m, the very top'
filled_in: Wheel size: 20 m spoke, angle measured up from level with the axle
Multiple-choice guess at 60° with 10, 13, 17 and 20 m options
Slider 0 to 90 degrees plus Turn to 30 and Turn to 60 buttons
Table of real height vs 'rises evenly' (10 m per 30 degrees) so the friend sees even growth would pass the top
Mirror-seat picture showing why 30 degrees gives exactly half (equilateral triangle)
SOH CAH TOA not repeated as a word; sine is explained as height divided by spoke

changed.what: The design said the friend thinks sin 60 would be 1 because sin goes up evenly; page uses the 'rises evenly' column to show that rule would put 90 degrees at 30 m, beyond the 20 m top
changed.why: Makes the wrong idea testable without staging it

math_check: Heights are measured from the drawn rider's pixel position (150 px = 20 m) and spoke length from the axle-to-seat distance. 30°: 10.0 m, ratio 0.50. 60°: 17.3 m, ratio 0.87. 90°: 20.0 m, 1.00. Table 15°: 5.2, 45°: 14.1, 75°: 19.3 m; even column 0,5,10,15,20,25,30 m. Mirror chord at ±30° = 20.0 m equals spoke.
